title: Main idea
examples: How can I tell the main idea from the topic?
What is the difference between a topic and the main idea?
If I find the main idea, what should I do next?

explain.say: Today we learn about the main idea of a text. Say the topic and the main idea are different things. The topic is just the general subject. The main idea is what the author wants you to learn.
The topic is a simple word or short phrase. Say it names the general subject matter. For example, the topic could be 'dogs' or 'recycling'.
The main idea is a whole sentence. Say it tells the reader the most important point. For instance, the main idea might be 'Dogs make wonderful pets'.
Supporting details help prove the main idea. Say these are the facts or examples given. They give us more information about the main point.
For example, if the main idea is 'Dogs make wonderful pets', supporting details could be 'They wag their tails' or 'They love to play fetch'.

items: Main Idea: Dogs are great pets

explain.say: In real life, think about a recipe you follow. Say the main idea is making delicious cookies. The supporting details are the amounts of flour and sugar you need.

faq.q: How do I know if a sentence is a supporting detail?
faq.a: A supporting detail gives a specific fact or example. It proves the main idea is true. You can also ask if it answers the 'how' or 'what' question.
asks: What is the difference between a fact and an idea?

faq.q: Can a text have more than one main idea?
faq.a: Most short texts have one main idea. If it seems to have many, you might need to read it in sections. Each section might have its own main idea.
asks: Does every paragraph have a main idea?
How many main ideas can I find?

faq.q: Is the main idea always in the first sentence?
faq.a: No, the main idea can be anywhere in the text. Sometimes it is in the middle or the end. You must read the whole passage to find it.
asks: Where should I look for the main idea?
Does the author always state the main idea?

faq.q: What if the topic is very broad, like 'space'?
faq.a: If the topic is broad, the main idea will narrow it down. For example, the main idea might be 'Mars is the most explored planet'.
asks: Can I find the main idea if the topic is big?
Does the main idea limit the topic?

faq.q: What is the difference between a topic and the main idea again?
faq.a: The topic is a single word or short phrase. The main idea is a complete sentence that tells the main message. Think of it as the subject versus the statement about the subject.
asks: Topic vs main idea: what is the difference?
Is the main idea a sentence?

facts: The topic is the general subject of the writing.
The main idea is the most important message the author wants you to know.
Supporting details are facts that help explain or prove the main idea.
The main idea is usually stated in a complete sentence.

quiz.say: The topic of a passage about dolphins is best described as:
quiz.why: The topic is just the subject, which is the word 'dolphins'.

wrong.0: This is a main idea, not just the topic.
wrong.1: This is a supporting detail, not the topic.
wrong.2: This is a specific fact, not the general topic.

quiz.say: If the main idea is 'Exercise is good for your heart', which of these is a supporting detail?

options.show: Exercise is good for your heart.
options.say: Exercise is good for your heart.

quiz.why: This is a specific fact that supports the main idea about heart health.

wrong.1: This is the main idea itself, not a detail.
wrong.2: This is a general fact about the heart, not a direct support for the main idea.
wrong.3: This is advice, not a specific supporting detail from the text.

quiz.say: Which of these sentences best states the main idea of a text about bees?

options.show: Bees are vital for growing many foods.
options.say: Bees are vital for growing many foods.

quiz.why: This sentence captures the most important message about bees.

wrong.1: This is a supporting detail, not the overall main idea.
wrong.2: This is another supporting detail about bee building.
wrong.3: This is just the topic, not a full sentence main idea.
